source: Rules of thumb used in first-pass protection arithmetic: long-term disability cover is sold to replace about 60% of gross pay; term life is sized at about ten times gross income when someone lives on it; a cash cushion of three months of spending is the floor and six months is the full cushion. None is a regulation or a quote.
confidenceNote: Every figure is a rule of thumb, and each has a range in practice: disability policies replace 50-70% of pay, life-cover multiples run from 7x to 15x depending on age and debts, and the cushion advice runs from three to twelve months. The room shows which it used; a real policy or a planner's number replaces it.
note: Shares are decimal fractions; multiples are ratios to gross annual income; months are months of a month's spending. Read by engines/protection.js. D-098.
